_about: Source data for wiki/counties/*.md and public/data/states/CO/hosting.json. Edit here, then run `python3 pipelines/hosting/build.py`. Claims are [text, [source ids]]. A source is primary when it is the government's own document (code, ordinance, official FAQ/form, statute); `read: true` means the cited text was read, not just summarized by a search.

Adams.summary: No camping-specific rule found. The code bars uses that aren't listed, so paid camping needs a written determination from Community & Economic Development.

code.title: Adams County Development Standards and Regulations

private: No camping-specific provision found in this pass.
commercial: Uses not listed as permitted or conditional are not allowed unless the Director finds them similar to a listed use. Ask for a written determination.
Adams.notes: Mostly suburban Front Range. Hipcamp's listing policy says residential/suburban homes generally aren't a fit.

Alamosa.summary: Paid camping means a campground/RV park: Special Use Permit on 12+ acres of Rural or Commercial land, with water and sewer. RV stays need an installed septic system.

faq.title: Alamosa County FAQ: Camping & RV Occupancy

private: Temporary/seasonal RV use: needs an installed, permitted OWTS and a legal water source. $125 permit, valid 180 days per calendar year.
faq
RV during home construction: OWTS, well and building permit required. $125, valid as long as the building permit.
faq
An RV, camper or tent may never be a permanent residence. The county enforces with fines and court filings.
faq
commercial: Campgrounds and RV parks need a Special Use Permit on Rural (RU) or Commercial (C) land of at least 12 acres. Temporary and permanent structures are allowed. Water and sewer infrastructure is required.
An earlier search reported a moratorium on campground SUPs. The current FAQ doesn't mention one. Confirm with Land Use.
Alamosa.notes: Septic comes first for any overnight stay. Commercial camping has a 12-acre minimum.

Chaffee.summary: Has a dedicated 'Commercial Private Lands Camping' license for agricultural properties: 5-acre minimum, 1 site per 5-10 ac, 2 sites per 10-20 ac, then about 1 per 20 ac, and a caretaker within 60 minutes.

luc.title: Chaffee County Land Use Code (eff. 1-1-2025, amended 9-16-2025)

res.title: Resolution 2022-67, Exhibit A (original ordinance text, hosted by NACo)

private: Vacant land: owners may camp up to 90 days (cumulative) per calendar year without a landowner camping permit.
luc
Improved property (a principal building with permanent water, wastewater, sanitary and refuse facilities): owners and 30+ day lessees may camp without limit, as long as it's not a nuisance.
luc
Camping equipment (tents, RVs, vans, park models, tiny homes not installed to DOH rules, yurts, tipis) can't be permanent habitation.
luc
commercial: Sec. 2.3.5.1 Commercial Private Lands Camping: a major accessory use license, only on properties whose principal use is agriculture or agritourism.
Density: 5-acre minimum. 5-9.99 ac: 1 site. 10-19.99 ac: 2 sites. 20-100 ac: 2 sites plus 1 per 20 ac. Over 100 ac: 1 per 20 ac. Acreage counts contiguous common ownership.
Owner or caretaker within a 60-minute drive whenever sites are occupied.

Sites: 900 sq ft (RV/van) or 600 sq ft (tent), cleared of vegetation. Setbacks: 50 ft from property lines, 100 ft from neighbors' dwellings, 100 ft from streams and wetlands, 50 ft from floodways. No sites in the 100-year floodplain, fluvial hazard areas or airport overlay.

Sanitation may be off-site (wag bags, RV tanks, portable toilets). Any onsite facility must be permitted under Reg 43. The fire protection district must approve site locations. Fire pits need a permanent structure with a grate.
Quiet hours 10pm-7am. Signs about fire bans, campfire safety, Leave No Trace and quiet hours. Seasonal closures in the top 50-100% of production/winter habitat.
The 2022 resolution also capped licenses at 10 campsites per ownership interest and required annual renewal. Confirm these carried into the 2025 code.
Chaffee.notes: The county code allows wag bags, but Hipcamp still requires a permitted toilet for tent camping on under 20 acres. Campgrounds and RV parks are a separate, heavier use (Table 2.1.3.4).

private: No camping-specific provision found in this pass.

Clear Creek.summary: Paid camping is 'Commercial Camping', allowed only in C-OR (up to 50 sites), C-TR or a Planned Development. 1-50 sites get an administrative permit. Sites must be 100 ft from existing homes, with access from a county-maintained road.

s21.title: Clear Creek County Zoning Regulations, Section 21 (Camping)

private: Private camping means no money or thing of value is exchanged. Allowed 14 days per year with no permit, plus 30 more days with a Private Camping Permit (approved sanitation required). Longer needs a Special Use Permit.
A new Private Camping Permit can't be issued until 30 days after the previous one expired.
commercial: Commercial Camping (money or value exchanged) is allowed only in Commercial-Outdoor Recreation (C-OR, max 50 sites), Commercial-Tourism Recreation (C-TR), or a Planned Development that includes it.
1-50 sites: Minor Camping Permit (administrative). 51+ sites: Major Camping Permit (public review).

Standards: nothing within 100 ft of an existing residence; 50 ft from streams (100 ft for structures/sanitary facilities); max 20 sites/acre; legal access from a county-maintained public road; animal-proof trash; no campgrounds in the 100-year floodplain; max 30 days per party per year.
Clear Creek.notes: Zoning comes first: most residential parcels would need rezoning to C-OR/C-TR.

Delta.summary: An RV connected to permanent water, wastewater and power can count as a dwelling here, which is unusual. Hauled-water cisterns generally aren't an adequate water supply for new development.
private: Not confirmed for camping specifically.
commercial: Not researched. Home businesses above the LUC thresholds move to Limited or Conditional Use review.
rv: One dwelling unit plus one ADU are Allowed Uses. A dwelling unit may be a house, cabin, mobile home or RV connected to permanent water, wastewater and electricity.
water: Wells must be permitted for the proposed use and can't serve other parcels without an augmentation plan. Hauled-water cisterns generally aren't an adequate supply for new development after Jan 5, 2021, with limited exceptions.
Delta.notes: No building codes in unincorporated Delta County (DOH list).

private: A tiny house on wheels is an RV, regulated by the Land Use Code, not the building code. RVs aren't permanent homes and can't be occupied year-round. They're temporary quarters for recreational, camping, travel or seasonal use, or a temporary dwelling during permitted construction.
faq

ldc.title: El Paso County Land Development Code

private: Occupying vehicles, including RVs, on private property isn't allowed. An RV may only be occupied while the permanent dwelling is built, with an active building permit and a temporary use permit.

commercial: Not researched. Check campground uses in the LDC use tables.

Fremont.summary: Tents and trailers can be occupied up to 3 months a year in R3 and 2 weeks in R1/R2/LDR/HDR, and not at all in business/industrial zones. Paid camping is a 'Campground' use.
private: Sec. 3.07: no trailer or tent may be occupied more than 3 months per year in R3, or 2 weeks per year in R1, R2, LDR and HDR. No camping in MHP, RHB, B, IP, I or AIP. Otherwise, using tents and trailers for habitation is prohibited.
zr
Agricultural districts aren't in the 3.07 table. Ask Planning how they're treated.
zr
A self-contained travel trailer may be a temporary dwelling during construction under an Agreement to Abate.
zr
commercial: 'Campground' means a tract developed for tent sites, travel trailers, RVs, campers, cabins and other temporary accommodations. Check the use table for which districts allow it and at what review level.

Garfield.summary: Has a 'Small Camping Facility' use for parcels of 10+ acres: operates May 1-Nov 30, with everything 200 ft from property lines. Larger operations are campgrounds/RV parks.

ludc.title: Garfield County Land Use and Development Code

private: Not confirmed.
commercial: 7-906 Small Camping Facility: only on properties of 10+ acres; only May 1-Nov 30; all facilities and activities at least 200 ft from the nearest property line; waterbody setbacks per 7-203; 2 passenger vehicles per tent pad or RV space; 1 RV per RV space.
7-905 covers larger Campground/RV Park uses. The site-count definitions and zone-district review levels are in the LUDC use tables and definitions.
Garfield.notes: The best fit for a small Hipcamp in western Colorado. Read the definition in Article 15 for the site cap.

Gilpin.summary: Renting campsites isn't a use by right anywhere in the county. Campgrounds need a Special Use in RR or commercial zones. Yurts, tiny homes and tents may not be rented out publicly.
private: Owners may camp on their property up to 30 days per calendar year with a camping permit.
pz
commercial: Public camping on private land, such as renting out campsites on vacant land, isn't a use by right in any zone district.
Campgrounds/RV parks can only be approved by Special Use in RR (Resource Residential) and commercial districts. The county recommends legal or planning help.
Temporary structures such as yurts, tiny homes and tents aren't permitted as permanent structures and may not be rented out publicly.

Grand.summary: 'Private camping' allows no compensation to the owner and 14 days in any 3 months. Camping areas are a special-review use in several districts.

zr.title: Grand County Zoning Regulations, Oct 2018 proposed amendment

zr
The cited text is a 2018 proposed amendment. Confirm the adopted Section 14.10.
commercial: 'Camping areas' are a Use Permitted by Special Review in the Accommodations, Forestry & Open, Tourist and Business districts. Spaces for motor homes, trailers and tents must be at least 1,500 sq ft.

ltc
lur

ldc

private: Owners may camp on their own land. No RV may be inhabited for any length of time without adequate sewage disposal.
prop
commercial: Hosting paid camping must meet the general campground/RV park regulations. 'Dry camping' for commercial gain is effectively banned.

Routt.summary: Commercial camping is a Special Use in Agriculture/Forestry. 1-3 spaces need a dump station, toilets and potable water. 4+ need hookups and showers. Ads must show the approval code.

udc.title: Routt County Unified Development Code (V5, eff. Jul 28, 2026)

private: Sec. 2.33: private non-commercial camping is only for the owner and invited, non-paying personal guests. Max 60 days cumulative per year; no permanent structures; no noise or light at the property line 10pm-7am; shelters removed when not in use.
udc
Sec. 2.34: extended private camping (61-180 days) needs a permit (M in the AF district).
udc
commercial: Sec. 2.35: Commercial Camping means one or more spaces open to the public, primitive or developed. It's a Special Use (S) in Agriculture/Forestry and allowed (R) in one other district. Check Table 2.22.G-1.

1-3 spaces: dump station plus toilets and potable water. 4+ spaces: 120/240V hookups, dump station, toilets, potable water, showers and screening landscaping. A 'dry campground' (no hookups) must prohibit dumping.
Must shield sites from public roads, use bear-proof trash, follow CDPHE 6 CCR 1010-9, and show the approval project code in all advertising.

Saguache.summary: You need a county-approved septic system to stay on the property. RV/camper/tent occupancy is tied to an active construction permit. Raw-land Hipcamp is unlikely.

docs.title: Saguache County Land Use Documents (Land Development Code)

private: A temporary RV permit requires a county-approved OWTS and an active construction permit. Valid for the construction permit's life (3 years).
docs
No RV, camper or tent may be a permanent residence. A county-approved septic system is needed to live or stay on the property.
docs

San Juan.summary: Reported: up to 20 days of camping a year without a permit. The Town of Silverton's rules are separate and still changing.

page.title: San Juan County Planning (Land Use Code revised Jul 10, 2023)

private: Reported (search summary): camping up to 20 days per year without a permit.
San Juan.notes: The Town of Silverton has its own RV/camper rules (workforce-RV ordinances; permit/sticker proposal, 2026).

San Miguel.summary: Camping is for the owner and guests, non-commercial. RVs, camping spaces and accessory structures can't be rented as short-term rentals. Campgrounds have their own standards.

faq.title: San Miguel County FAQ: Camping on Private Property

luc.title: San Miguel County Land Use Code (Sec. 5-714, 5-1008, 5-1009)

cp.title: Citizen Portal: new rules for private camping and campgrounds

private: Non-commercial tents/RVs may be used by the landowner or guests for recreation or vacation (LUC 5-714). Beyond 14 days in a calendar quarter, only one RV or temporary shelter per property at a time.
faq
More than one unit for over 14 days in a quarter needs a Temporary Use Permit (5-301 A).
faq
commercial: 'The rental of accessory structures, recreational vehicles, camping spaces, and other spaces not located in the primary dwelling unit is not allowed as a Short-Term Rental.'
Separate standards for RV parks, trailer parks, commercial campgrounds and semi-primitive campgrounds (5-1008, 5-1009), adopted on a split vote.

Sedgwick.summary: No camping-specific rule found. No county building department.
private: No camping-specific provision found in this pass.

ludc.title: Summit County Land Use and Development Code

private: Not found in this pass. (County open space rules cover public land only.)

Teller.summary: Owners may camp up to 60 days a year. A $25 permit is needed for 14+ days on vacant land. Paid camping wasn't researched.
private: Owners may camp on their property up to 60 days in any 12-month period. A $25 permit is needed for 14+ days on vacant property.
ord
koaa
A camping unit is an RV, camp trailer, 5th wheel or tent. Trash must be managed onsite. Longer stays need septic, water and a TUP.
ord
Teller.notes: The ordinance PDF is a scan (not text-searchable). Planning: 719-687-3048.

Washington.summary: No camping-specific rule found. Land-use changes go through the Planning Commission and BOCC.
private: Not confirmed. More than one residence on under 35 acres needs health-department septic approval.
page
commercial: Changes of land use go to the Planning Commission, then the BOCC.

Weld.summary: 'Camping' is capped at 7 consecutive nights. A 'campground' is commercial RV/tent use for the public. Check the zone-district use lists.

code.title: Weld County Charter and County Code, Ch. 23 (Zoning)

ag.title: Weld County A-zone guide (lots outside subdivisions)

private: 'Camping' means up to 7 consecutive nights in a tent, primitive structure, travel trailer or RV at a campsite. Temporary shelter, not a residence.
code
commercial: 'Campground' means an area for temporary RV/tent placement, operated commercially for the public. Check the A-district use lists.

Yuma.summary: The 2024 Land Use Code regulates RV storage and use in residential districts. Details not confirmed.
private: The code regulates storage, parking and use of RVs and campers in residential districts. Details not confirmed.
luc
Yuma.notes: No county building department. Watch for Yuma County, Arizona results when searching.
